children.value: Sometimes you just need someone to talk to.
Real-time voice conversations with strangers, where both people choose to talk. Nobody sees your name, number or profile. They only know what you choose to say.
Free private beta on Android and iOS, in the US. We'll only use your email for beta news. You can unsubscribe anytime.
Have something on your mind? Share it. Want to be there for someone? Listen. Or just talk. It's not a dating app, just conversation.

suggests that talking with strangers leaves people feeling more connected than they expect. But everyday life offers fewer chances to do it, and social media doesn't fill the gap: online contact with people you've never met is linked to
Record a short spoken intro and choose some optional preferences to help us match you with another user.
When you're free, you can choose to mark yourself as available for calls and/or listen to other people's intros and initiate a call yourself.
When receiving a call, users will hear the intro for the person calling them and can decide then whether or not they are interested.

To keep everyone safe, calls are securely recorded and may be reviewed if someone reports a problem. Recordings are deleted after 30 days unless a report needs them and only ever reviewed when reported.
Twyne is for adults 18+ and is not a substitute for professional mental health support. In a crisis, seek
The private beta is free. Beta users who stay active get a lifetime discount and a few free months when we launch. We'll only use your email for beta news.
Twyne is for adults 18 and over. Nobody under 18 may use it. Twyne does not allow child sexual abuse or exploitation of any kind.
Twyne bans child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE), including:
describing, offering, asking for or sharing child sexual abuse material, in any form
grooming a child, or trying to contact, meet or get images from anyone under 18
sexual talk about children, in a call or in an intro
using Twyne to arrange, advertise or encourage the abuse of children
Anyone who breaks these rules is banned, and we report it to the authorities as the law requires.
Everyone confirms they're 18 or over when they sign up.
You can't send photos, videos, files or messages on Twyne.
Nobody sees your name, number or profile. Every call goes through Twyne's servers, so nobody learns your phone number or IP address.
Every spoken intro is checked before anyone else hears it. Intros that seem to include contact details wait for a person to review them.
Every call starts with an announcement that it is recorded, so reports can be checked. Recordings are deleted after 30 days unless a report needs them.
during or after a call, tap Report and choose "They seem to be under 18" or "Sexual content." Reports that someone seems to be under 18 go to the front of our review queue.
If a child is in immediate danger, call
. You can also report child sexual exploitation to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) at
A member of our safety team listens to the reported call and reads its transcript.
We can suspend or ban the person. Bans are tied to their phone number, so making a new account on the same number doesn't get around a ban.
If we find child sexual abuse material or evidence that a child is being exploited, we keep the evidence, report it to NCMEC as US law requires, and work with law enforcement.
If we learn that someone using Twyne is under 18, we suspend their account.
